name: Should I use custom cabinetry in a small kitchen?

mainEntity.name: When does custom cabinetry make more sense than semi-custom in tight Los Angeles spaces?
mainEntity.text: When does custom cabinetry make more sense than semi-custom in tight Los Angeles spaces?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a small kitchen, custom cabinetry can be a major advantage because it lets the design use awkward corners, full-height storage, and appliance clearances more efficiently. That matters in many Los Angeles homes where kitchens are compact or have been remodeled multiple times. Custom work is especially valuable when the room has uneven walls, limited ceiling height, or a need for hidden storage that standard cabinet sizes cannot provide. However, if the layout is straightforward and standard cabinet dimensions work well, semi-custom may achieve a similar look with less cost and lead time. The decision usually comes down to whether the space benefits from precise fit and integrated details. If storage, alignment, and finish cohesion are priorities, custom cabinetry often earns its price. If the project is mostly cosmetic, semi-custom can be the smarter value.
acceptedAnswer.description: Custom cabinetry makes sense in small kitchens when every inch matters, appliances need exact integration, or the room has unusual walls, soffits, or plumbing constraints. It can create better storage than standard sizes. Semi-custom may be enough if the layout is simple and the cabinet dimensions already fit well.
